Gil enters the building, noting the wet floors.  He pulls out the book he writes all his notes in.  A book that has been mostly unused the last couple of days.  He begins writing a note, and when done, he copies it so it can be posted to another place.

```It has come to my attention, that the town is in dire straights.  The flooding likely wont end, and if we do not invest in being able to move, all of our production, and potentially our lives, may be lost.  We have two days to get 30 days worth of labor, and 20,000 gold in materials.  I will not support us subjugating the local tribes to make this happen.  We have only a few options.
1) We can see if one of the local tribes will give us aid, but we have to align with their causes.
2) We can ask for aid from multiple tribes, and owe them a undefined favor down the road that may get us in worse waters
With these two options, it falls on Viola to contact the tribes we decide on to get the aid we need.

There is another option.  When I proposed a council, it was with the understanding that we are all equals in this community.  We work together for a better tomorrow.  We unify.  The Aristocracy cannot be the only ones funding the projects the town needs to survive.  We have spent what we can this last week and a half seeding this community and getting it on its feet.  Its time everyone takes ownership of our problems.  Ultimately, I can't make anyone do anything, and organizing labor is Copper's duty.  But if you want us to survive, and possibly thrive, its time to to work as one.  The counsel will have to vote today, on which of the diplomatic options we will seek if any.  But if you the people want to lessen that burden, and save your way of life, speak up, and let us know how you can help.

It is long past time for us to shoulder the weight together.```
